question: How is the Brahmāṇḍa divided by the outer and intermediate groups in this enumeration?
premises: The sequence extends upward through named lords up to Śambhu.
The outer division is associated with eleven.
The intermediate division is associated with five.
inference: The Brahmāṇḍa is structured here by an outer group of eleven and an intermediate group of five within the named hierarchy.
uncertainties: The compound laghunidhipatividyādhipaśambhūrdhvāntaṃ compresses several names whose exact boundaries are interpretive.
plain_english: The sequence runs upward through the named lords as far as Śambhu, together with the lord of Vīrabhadra. In the outer division of the Brahmāṇḍa there are eleven, and likewise five in the intermediate division.
